requirements.statement: On every CI lane, a differential oracle MUST ask the kernel at least 1,000 generated questions per preset and target, reaching every rule kind (allow, protect, hide, hard-deny class, base, default, grant, T1 cover), for every operation listed as proven, and MUST fail naming the question on any disagreement; a lane that cannot confine its children MUST fail, never skip.

acceptance.given: the oracle suite on each lane
acceptance.then: every rule kind is reached, at least 1,000 questions per preset and target are asked, and all agree

acceptance.given: an evaluator mutated to flip the decision of one rule kind
acceptance.then: it fails and names a question of that kind

acceptance.given: a lane that is itself sandboxed
acceptance.then: it fails with AlreadySandboxed

requirements.statement: The oracle MUST ask a caged child on every lane and classify its observed result as allowed (success), denied (EACCES, EPERM, EROFS) or unresolved (anything else, including ENOENT for a file the generator made), and MUST fail on an unresolved question rather than count it as agreement.

acceptance.given: a question whose open fails with ENOENT or another unexpected errno
acceptance.then: the suite fails naming the question

acceptance.given: any lane
acceptance.then: it uses a caged child's observed open or execve result, never sandbox_check

requirements.statement: A question MUST carry the target, the Linux tier, the per-spawn grants and the homes; on Linux an answer that holds only for paths existing at spawn (class covers on T1, piecewise hides on T2) MUST say so with the limit, never a plain denied.

acceptance.given: a trust-handoff name under a writable tree on T1
acceptance.then: the answer is denied by that class with the spawn caveat, and the oracle agrees for a file that existed at spawn
acceptance.when: a write to a file in it is explained

acceptance.given: a path outside the policy and a grant for it
acceptance.then: it is allowed by the grant with it and denied by the deciding rule without it, as the kernel observes
acceptance.when: it is explained with and without the grant

requirements.statement: A remedy MUST be the narrowest change for the deciding rule (a literal rule of the asked access for the path asked, a waiver by class only when a hard-deny class decides, the removal of the deciding protect or hide rule), MUST be offered only when re-lowering confirms it flips the question, and MUST carry the diff of the change so it names every other question it also flips.

acceptance.given: every generated denied question of a preset
acceptance.then: the question flips and the diff equals the remedy's diff
acceptance.when: its remedy is applied and the old and new policies are diffed

acceptance.given: a write to .git/hooks/x
acceptance.then: the answer is denied by hard deny trust-handoff, the remedy is that waiver, and no subpath rule

requirements.statement: explain MUST accept only a canonical absolute path: a relative path, dot or dot-dot components, repeated separators, a trailing separator and the macOS alias spellings MUST return an error naming the canonical form; Cage::explain MUST resolve symbolic links on the host first; pattern characters in a question path MUST stay literal.

acceptance.given: /etc/hosts on macOS and /a/../b
acceptance.then: each is an error naming /private/etc/hosts and /b

acceptance.given: a symbolic link to a protected file
acceptance.then: the answer is about the file it resolves to
acceptance.when: Cage::explain is asked about the link
